@@U02418@@
(To the CROWD. )

@@U02419@@
I have strewn among you my finest gifts. On this head and that I see glowing a tiny flame I sparked into life. It leaps lightly from one to another; on this head it lingers, on others not, and only rarely does it flare up and in a brief flowering illuminate all around it. Sadly, on most, it dies out, unrecognized.

@@U02421@@
—Do you see? —Up there? —On the chariot? —A charlatan! —And behind him a clown! —I’ve never seen him so thin! —Skin and bones! —Pinch him, he'd never feel it!

@@U02423@@
Women! Ah! They disgust me! Keep them away! I know I’ll never suit them! In days when women ran the house, my name was Madam Avarice. Things were well run then, house in good order, much coming 1n, nothing going out! I kept a sharp eye on chests and cupboards
translation:
@@U02418@@
（致人群。）

@@U02419@@
我已将我最好的礼物撒在你们中间。在这个头上，我看到它闪烁着我点燃的生命的微小火焰。它轻轻地从一个跳到另一个；它在这个头上徘徊，在其他头上则不然，而且很少会突然爆发并在短暂的开花中照亮周围的一切。可悲的是，在大多数情况下，它消失了，未被认识到。

@@U02421@@
——你看到了吗？ ——在上面吗？ ——战车上？ ——江湖骗子！ ——他身后有一个小丑！ ——我从来没见过他这么瘦过！ ——皮肤和骨头！ ——掐他一下，他根本感觉不到！

@@U02423@@
女人！啊!他们令我厌恶！让他们远离！我知道我永远不会适合他们！在妇女掌管家务的时代，我的名字叫贪婪女士。那时一切都运转良好，家里秩序井然，来了很多，没有出去！我密切关注箱子和橱柜
